blueprint_topic: Management of Care — informed shared decision-making for durable LVAD destination therapy
stem: A client with advanced heart failure is considering a durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) as destination therapy. Which nursing action best supports informed shared decision-making?

options.A: Explore the client's goals, reinforce balanced education about expected benefits and long-term device burdens, and bring unresolved questions to the LVAD team.
options.B: Emphasize medical eligibility and expected survival benefit, then defer discussion of device burdens unless the client decides against implantation.
options.C: Ask the family to identify the preferred treatment first, then use that preference to guide the information presented to the client about the device.
options.D: Focus teaching on postoperative device care after the decision is made because detailed risk and lifestyle information is primarily part of surgical consent.

rationale: A is correct. The 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline describes shared decision-making as a process in which patients and clinicians use unbiased evidence about benefits, risks, burdens, and alternatives together with the patient's goals and informed preferences. In the durable mechanical-circulatory-support section, the guideline notes that LVAD support can improve survival, functional status, and health-related quality of life but also involves an external-device lifestyle burden and substantial rehospitalization/complication risk; these factors support thorough multidisciplinary evaluation and patient education before proceeding. B is incorrect because emphasizing benefit while deferring burdens is not balanced informed decision-making. C is incorrect because family input may support care, but the client's own values and informed preferences remain central to the decision when the client can participate. D is incorrect because device burdens, risks, and lifestyle implications are relevant before the treatment decision and should not be postponed until after implantation is chosen.
educational_objective: Support durable-LVAD decisions by eliciting the client's goals and preferences, reinforcing balanced information about benefits, risks and long-term burdens, and coordinating unanswered questions with the multidisciplinary LVAD team before the decision is finalized.
source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America
source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure
source_version_date: Originally published April 1, 2022 with subsequent corrections; current ACC Heart Failure Guideline Hub still lists the 2022 guideline, and ACC Clinical Policy in Progress updated June 15, 2026 schedules the Heart Failure guideline update for 2027; sources rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: Section 8.4 — Mechanical Circulatory Support, Synopsis/Recommendation-Specific Supportive Text: durable LVAD support has improved functional status and health-related quality of life in trials; destination-therapy MCS provides survival advantage and improvement in functional status/QOL in appropriate advanced-HF patients; external power/driveline burden and frequent rehospitalization/complications emphasize thorough evaluation and patient education before proceeding; appropriate selection benefits from multidisciplinary review including HF cardiology, surgery, nursing, pharmacy, social work, nutrition, and palliative medicine. Section 13.1 — Shared decision-making: patients and clinicians make decisions from medically reasonable options using unbiased evidence about risks, benefits, burdens, and alternatives together with patient goals and informed preferences. ACC currentness sources: 2022 HF Guideline Hub; Clinical Policy in Progress updated June 15, 2026 lists HF guideline update for 2027.
source_claim_supported: Current HF guidance supports multidisciplinary pre-LVAD education and values-based shared decision-making that addresses potential survival/function/QOL benefits together with device-related burdens, risks, alternatives, and the patient's goals/preferences before durable LVAD implantation.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Client Rights/Advocacy/Informed Consent/Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team: support client participation in decisions, advocate for client needs and preferences, provide or reinforce information within nursing scope, identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members, and communicate unresolved questions or concerns to the appropriate team member.

The HF guideline was verified through current HTML/ACC pages; no guideline PDF is relied upon for this item.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'LVAD destination therapy shared decision making benefits burdens patient goals education multidisciplinary' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the cueable LVAD item into a balanced RN shared-decision action. The revised options test realistic errors involving benefit-heavy counseling, substituting family preference for the client's informed preference, and delaying burden/risk education until after the decision, while keeping eligibility and prescribing decisions with the advanced-HF/LVAD team.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly combines patient goals/preferences, balanced education, and multidisciplinary clarification before the treatment decision.
option_audit.B: Plausible benefit-framing error; incorrect because shared decision-making requires balanced discussion of benefits, risks, burdens, and alternatives rather than delaying burdens.
option_audit.C: Plausible family-centered error; incorrect because the competent client's goals and informed preferences remain central, although family support may be included.
option_audit.D: Plausible consent-timing error; incorrect because LVAD burdens, risks, and lifestyle implications are part of pre-decision education and evaluation.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four options contain comparable decision-support detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel nursing actions within the same pre-LVAD decision construct.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ACC/HFSA source-based reread.
